protocol.name: nidara_window_controls_v1

description.summary: window controls drawn by the compositor over an app's header

protocol.description: A window's controls — close, minimize, maximize — are the compositor's: it draws them, the same in every window, and takes their clicks. The app keeps its own header and its content, and says where in it the controls go: it reserves a box of the size the compositor gives, at the place its layout wants (in the header, or inside a sidebar), and the compositor draws the controls there, over the app's own pixels. The place can move with the layout; the side (left or right) is the user's, and the compositor tells it.

request.name: get_window_controls

description.summary: the controls of a toplevel's surface

request.description: One per wl_surface, which must have the xdg_toplevel role (or get it before its first commit with a position). The state is double-buffered on wl_surface.commit, so the controls move with the buffer that leaves room for them.

event.name: layout

description.summary: the box to reserve, and the side it belongs on

event.description: Sent once right after get_window_controls, and again whenever the user changes the side or the compositor changes the controls' size. width and height are the box the controls take, logical pixels; the client lays out a box of that size on that side and sends its position. On the left side the close button comes first; on the right, last.

description.summary: the compositor draws no controls on this surface any more

request.name: set_position
request.description: The top-left corner of the reserved box, surface-local logical coordinates. Until the first set_position, and after unset_position, no controls are drawn.
